ourClaims.timeToEffect: Acute effects within 1–2 hours; optimal at 4–6 weeks

humanEffects.notes: One of the best-evidenced acute cognitive effects in the nootropic category.
Significant improvements in digit span and working memory tasks.
fMRI studies confirm increased frontal lobe ATP production.
Strongest effects in stroke recovery and TBI models; effects in healthy adults are maintenance-level.

studies.title: Cytidinediphosphocholine (CDP-choline) for cognitive and behavioural disturbances associated with chronic cerebral disorders in the elderly
studies.population: elderly with chronic cerebral disorders (subjective memory disorders through vascular dementia)
studies.duration: 20 days to 12 months across included trials
studies.outcome: attention, memory, behaviour, global clinical impression
studies.result: No evidence of benefit on attention; positive effect on memory function and behaviour in short-to-medium term; drug well tolerated.

studies.title: Is Citicoline Effective in Preventing and Slowing Down Dementia? – A Systematic Review and a Meta-Analysis
studies.population: mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, post-stroke dementia
studies.dose: not stated in abstract (7 studies pooled, 6 in meta-analysis)
studies.result: Positive effect on cognitive status; pooled SMD 0.56 (95% CI 0.37–0.75) to 1.57 (95% CI 0.77–2.37) across sensitivity analyses. Overall study quality rated poor with significant risk of bias favoring the intervention.

studies.title: Citicoline improves verbal memory in aging
studies.population: healthy older adults 50–85y, subgroup with relatively inefficient memory
studies.result: Citicoline improved delayed recall in subjects with inefficient memory (parallel study); higher 2000mg dose associated with improved immediate and delayed memory (crossover study).

studies.title: A randomized dose-response trial of citicoline in acute ischemic stroke patients
studies.population: acute ischemic stroke patients (21 US centers)
studies.outcome: functional outcome (Barthel Index, Rankin), NIH stroke scale, Mini-Mental Status Exam
studies.result: Favorable functional outcome and reduced neurologic deficit with citicoline; 500mg identified as optimal dose; no drug-related serious adverse events.

studies.title: Improvements in concentration, working memory and sustained attention following consumption of a natural citicoline-caffeine beverage
studies.journal: International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition
studies.dose: citicoline-caffeine beverage (citicoline dose not isolated in abstract)
studies.outcome: maze learning time, reaction time, go/no-go accuracy, EEG P450 amplitude
studies.result: Faster maze learning and reaction times, fewer go/no-go errors, higher P450 amplitude (sustained attention/working memory) vs. placebo. Citicoline was co-administered with caffeine, so the effect cannot be attributed to citicoline alone.

studies.title: The Real-World Early Neuroprotective Effects of Oral Citicoline Combination in Prodromal Dementia
studies.design: retrospective, observational, real-world cohort study (not randomized)
studies.population: prodromal dementia / early Alzheimer's-type cognitive decline, 100 patients + 50 age-matched healthy controls
studies.dose: oral citicoline combined preparation (specific mg not stated in abstract)
studies.outcome: executive function, processing speed, working memory, visuospatial/verbal memory, fluency, mood
studies.result: Improvements across multiple cognitive domains and mood outcomes (p<0.05, most p<0.001) vs. baseline/controls. Authors explicitly call findings exploratory, requiring RCT confirmation given the observational design.

verdicts.claim: Attention & Focus — strong evidence, moderate magnitude, 8 studies
verdicts.reason: The Cochrane meta-analysis explicitly found 'no evidence of a beneficial effect of CDP-choline on attention' in its target population (PMID 15846601). The only acute healthy-adult attention RCT retrieved (PMID 25046515) used citicoline co-administered with caffeine, so citicoline's isolated contribution to attention cannot be determined from it. 'Strong' evidence for a clean attention effect is not supported by the strongest study type (meta-analysis) retrieved.

verdicts.claim: Working Memory — moderate evidence, moderate magnitude, 6 studies
verdicts.reason: Spiers 1996 (PMID 8624220) shows a genuine verbal/working-memory benefit in older adults with inefficient memory, and the Bonvicini 2023 meta-analysis (PMID 36678257) shows a positive pooled cognitive effect, though both are in older/clinical populations rather than general healthy adults and both flag caveats (small effect subgroup in Spiers; poor overall study quality in Bonvicini).

verdicts.claim: Brain Energy Metabolism — moderate evidence, moderate magnitude, 4 studies, 'fMRI studies confirm increased frontal lobe ATP production'
verdicts.reason: No fMRI/31P-MRS ATP-production RCT for citicoline was located in this search (PubMed RCT, meta-analysis, and systematic-review queries). This claim could not be verified or refuted with the sources retrieved.

verdicts.claim: Neuroprotection — moderate evidence, large magnitude, 5 studies, 'strongest in stroke recovery and TBI models'
verdicts.reason: Stroke neuroprotection is supported by Clark 1997 (PMID 9305321), a genuine dose-response RCT showing functional benefit. No TBI-specific citicoline RCT was retrieved in this search to support the 'TBI models' half of the claim — this is a gap, not a confirmation, and should not be asserted as supporting evidence without a located trial.

doseAssessment.trialRange: 500mg/day (optimal dose, acute stroke RCT) up to 1000–2000mg/day (memory RCTs in older adults)
doseAssessment.suggestedText: 250–500mg/day sits at the low end of studied doses. The stroke dose-response trial identified 500mg as optimal (2000mg was not superior), but the memory-focused RCT in older adults used 1000–2000mg/day. Current copy doesn't distinguish that higher doses were used in the strongest memory trial.

safetySignals.signal: No new safety signal identified beyond what the page already states (rare headache, insomnia if taken late). None of the retrieved trials reported drug-related serious adverse events; Clark 1997 explicitly notes no drug-related serious adverse events or deaths.

gaps: No fMRI/ATP-metabolism citicoline study located to support the 'Brain Energy Metabolism' claim.
No dedicated TBI RCT for citicoline located; our copy's neuroprotection claim implies TBI-model support that this search could not confirm.
No healthy-adult RCT of citicoline alone (without caffeine co-administration) was found for the acute attention claim.
The 1–2 hour acute onset claim is not directly demonstrated by any retrieved human RCT measuring cognition at that exact timepoint; it is plausible from choline pharmacokinetics but unverified here.
